correctness.rationale: For all odd q, exact parity reduction gives [a,b]=2(u wedge v+u wedge beta+alpha wedge v), with q^16 free even coefficients. A nonzero simple bivector has q(q^2-1) vector-pair preimages; the top functional on the eight triple-coefficients is surjective for every nonzero vector pair, hence each top fiber has q^7 choices. The zero-wedge pair count is 1+(q^4-1)(q+1), with the unique zero pair contributing q^8 only to the zero top fiber. These exhaust all cases and prove the image, count, probability, and width-two statement. The packaged verifier checks all 43,046,721 odd-input pairs over F3 and independent full Grassmann products over F3/F5. Experiments corroborate but do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: For four generators (first dimension permitting rank-four nonsimple bivectors), the map of ordinary commutators has a proper nonlinear Pluecker image despite a full seven-dimensional linear span, so image-versus-span is a substantive algebraic distinction. Every output fiber is classified over all odd finite fields, with exceptional central-axis multiplicities, exact commuting probability and sharp two-summand width. This is a natural complete classification, rather than a numerical slice, and can serve as an exact baseline for higher exterior ranks.
